## Summary

Implements the first refactor and the executable architecture contracts from #103.

```text
proposal preparation
  replay and verify the snapshot
  derive the release plan once
  render the changelog and prepare files from the same evidence
```

Planning, changelog rendering, configuration, and proposal preparation have dedicated modules. Reading automation configuration no longer loads proposal reconciliation. The published entry points and installed producer module paths remain compatible.

## Release context

```release-log
version: 1
audience: internal
summary: "Reuse verified release evidence during proposal preparation and enforce TypeScript architecture boundaries."
impact: "Contributors get a named check when an import crosses a release capability boundary or creates a runtime cycle."
required_action: null
```

## Verification and evidence

- The pre-commit hook ran `pnpm check`, including formatting, lint, strict type checking, architecture contracts, the behavioral suite, and the documentation build.
- The architecture fixtures cover direct, indirect, and type-only boundary violations. A runtime triangle with shorter type-only paths reproduced a false pass on a combined graph. Checking cycles on the runtime graph catches it.
- Proposal preparation tests compare generated files with expected bytes, including canonical snapshot serialization and preserved released history. The packed CLI and installed-producer tests exercise compatibility.

## Risks and limitations

The refactor is reversible. Changes to proposal preparation affect every generated release, so byte-level and installed-package tests cover the main risk. Dependency-cruiser has a separately locked TypeScript 6 installation because the root lockfile contributes to replay identity. A fresh architecture check needs registry access or a populated pnpm cache.

## Summary

Stacked on #108. Implements the publication portion of #103.

```text
approved evidence + observed tag, release, assets and images
  → plan ordered actions
  → execute one GitHub write
  → inspect again and confirm progress
```

Publication policy decoding, registry observation, local asset verification, and GitHub writes now have dedicated modules. A dependency-cruiser contract keeps transport and filesystem imports out of the planner, including indirect and type-only dependencies.

## Evidence

The previous 1,090-line module now provides the existing public package entry point in 15 lines. Verification passed with four CPUs available to Node, including 823 behavioral tests and 14 architecture tests. The packaged CLI also passed independently after hitting its 90-second limit during unrestricted parallel runs. Verified the built publication exports and error identity.

## Merge Danger

**Door** — Two-way. Reverting restores the previous implementation.

**Blast radius** — Publication. Recovery depends on preserving the order of reads and writes. The controlled transport tests cover uncertain writes, remote changes, and approval edits between actions.

## Release context

```release-log
version: 1
audience: internal
summary: Separate publication planning from registry observation and GitHub writes.
impact: Maintainers can review recovery decisions independently and check their dependency boundary automatically.
required_action: null
```

pullRequests.body:
## Summary

Stacked on #110. The 812-line snapshot entry point handled capture, evidence validation, replay, and tool identity. Internal callers now import the module that owns each operation. Installed producers can still load the original entry point.

```text
src/
├── release-snapshot.ts          # producer-facing exports
└── snapshot/
    ├── capture.ts               # normalize evidence into a release snapshot
    ├── replay.ts                # verify and serialize captured snapshots
    ├── evidence.ts              # decode association evidence
    ├── graph.ts                 # validate commit ancestry and release membership
    └── runtime-identity.ts      # derive the normalizer identity from pinned inputs
```

The dependency-cruiser contract rejects transitive imports from snapshot code into planning, proposal, changelog, or publication. Its regression fixture includes a type-only edge.

## Release context

```release-log
version: 1
audience: internal
summary: "Separate snapshot capture and replay behind the existing producer entry point."
impact: "Maintainers can change snapshot validation independently of downstream release workflows."
required_action: null
```

## Verification

- Ran `pnpm verify` with Node 26.13.1 on the stacked branch.
- Built the CLI and compared three snapshot fixtures against #110 through both source and compiled entry points. Each produced identical bytes and replayed the baseline snapshot.

## Risks and limitations

Historical producers load modules by path. The compatibility entry point and its named exports remain available. Runtime identity reads the manifest and dependency lock relative to its new location, which the compiled replay comparison exercises. Reverting this commit restores the previous layout.

pullRequests.body:
## Summary

Stacked on #113 as the proposal slice of #103. The reconciler previously inspected history, decided the result, wrote Git objects, moved the branch, and saved the PR in one function. `src/proposal/` now owns these steps.

```text
reconcileReleaseProposal
  inspectProposalHistory      verify prior cycles and adoption evidence
  prepareVerifiedRelease      compute intended file changes
  writeProposal               recheck freshness, verify the new tree, update the ref and PR
```

Proposal identity, prior-proposal verification, and local filesystem access have dedicated modules. The result type now guarantees a proposal ID, pull number, and head SHA after callers narrow to `created` or `refreshed`. Dependency-cruiser enforces direct imports from owning modules and restricts the history and write phases to reconciliation.

## Release context

```release-log
version: 1
audience: internal
summary: "Separate proposal history verification and guarded writes within the proposal lifecycle."
impact: "Maintainers can review each remote mutation in one place and rely on precise result types after a successful write."
required_action: null
```

## Verification

- Ran `pnpm verify` on Node 26.13.1, including behavior, strict types, architecture fixtures, and the documentation build.
- Compared all six serialized outcomes and the ordered GitHub request traces against #113 with deterministic local Git fixtures.
- Built the CLI and exercised both branches as active and pinned producers. Reconstructed snapshots, prepared files, and proposal descriptions matched.

## Risks and limitations

The highest-risk path is a remote change between commit creation, branch update, and PR save. Freshness checks still run at those boundaries, and the existing controlled race and partial-write tests exercise them. The package entry point and producer-loaded file paths remain available. TypeScript consumers that previously extended the result interface must use a type intersection with the new result union. The shared GitHub adapter and foundational path policy still serve several capabilities. This commit can be reverted independently.

```text
cycle/select → cycle/history
             → tagging/reconcile → tagging/evidence
```

Cycle selection owns ancestry and merged-proposal ordering. Tag reconciliation owns freshness checks and the guarded tag write. Read-side helpers accept only the repository operations they use. Dependency-cruiser rejects internal imports through the root compatibility modules.

## Release context

summary: "Move release cycle selection and tag reconciliation into capability directories."
impact: "Maintainers can inspect ancestry decisions separately from tag freshness and write checks."
required_action: null

- Compared all 13 existing function bodies in cycle selection and tagging against the merged baseline.
- Ran the full repository check, including the controlled GitHub and Git integration suites and architecture fixtures.

## Merge Danger

**Door** — two-way. The public entry points retain their existing exports.

**Blast radius** — cycle selection and tag reconciliation, including retries around concurrent remote changes.

pullRequests.body:
## Summary

Tagged release cycles can stop when GitHub reports one landing SHA for a stack and the PR targeting the release branch has a different head from the merge's second parent.

```text
Shared landing on the release branch
  Verify the PR chain and complete Git footprint
  Assign every commit to one PR and recheck ownership on replay
  Plan from each PR's title, release context, and owned commits
```

Closes #119.

## Release context

```release-log
version: 1
audience: users
summary: "Support verified stacked pull requests in tagged release cycles."
impact: "Rolling releases account for every commit in a verified stack and retain each pull request's changelog entry, version impact, and migration instructions. A stack without releasable changes stays in range for the next release."
required_action: null
```

## Evidence

- Before this change, the rolling release after `v0.5.0` failed with `PR #108 merge parents do not match its captured head.` [Failed workflow run](https://github.com/lhajoosten/release-log/actions/runs/44834363253)
- The issue branch replayed both reported landings using real Git history and recorded PR evidence. It accounted for 17 commits across seven PRs and returned no release. GitHub's anonymous API rate limit interrupted the separate live check.

## Verification

- `pnpm verify` passed on Node 26.13.1, including 833 tests, architecture checks, and the docs build.
- The rolling release integration tests cover a refactor-only stack followed by a fix, per-PR bumps and breaking actions, and rejection of missing, competing, or partial evidence.

## Merge Danger

**Door** — Two-way. The collector change can be reverted. A snapshot containing stack evidence requires a producer that supports that evidence.

**Blast radius** — Collection. The new path applies to tagged cycles with a verified same-repository stack. Partial or contradictory evidence stops collection.

## Summary

Pin the reusable workflow and CLI to the same reviewed main revision, `a4b2a83`, which contains the stacked-landing collector from #120.

## Evidence

[The roll after #120](https://github.com/lhajoosten/release-log/actions/runs/44842858737/job/136655301099#step:11:17) checked out the older `8ca6913` pin and failed on PR #108’s merge parents. [Main Quality passed for `a4b2a83`](https://github.com/lhajoosten/release-log/actions/runs/44842858296). Local actionlint passed for the changed caller. The pinned source includes stacked landing handling and its producer chain retains the v0.5.0 proposal producer.

## Merge Danger

Two-way. The caller pins can be reverted in a subsequent review. Check the new run after main Quality succeeds. Retrying an old run preserves its original workflow revision.

```release-log
version: 1
audience: internal
summary: Activate the reviewed stacked-landing collector in the rolling release workflow.
impact: The release workflow can use the merged fix when collecting the current cycle.
required_action: null
```
